newsitem.title: USA: Ashrawi accuses US mediator of bias toward Israel.
newsitem.headline: Ashrawi accuses US mediator of bias toward Israel.

text.p: Hanan Ashrawi, a senior official of Yasser Arafat's Palestinian Authority, accused U.S. mediator Dennis Ross on Friday of abandoning his neutrality and showing bias toward Israel, the Washington Post reported.

The newspaper quoted Ashrawi as saying Ross's suggestion that Israel and the Palestinians agree to a withdrawal of Israeli troops from the occupied West Bank in 1998 amounted to a compromise that favoured Israel.

Israel had agreed to withdraw its troops from the West Bank by September 1997, but Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu this week proposed delaying the transfer to the Palestinian Authority until May 1999.
Ross is in the region for talks with both sides on the delayed transfer.
Ashrawi, Minister for Higher Education in Arafat's government, said Ross proposed the two sides split the difference and suggested a date in 1998.
"A mediator should offer compromise before an agreement is signed, not after," the Post quoted Ashrawi as telling reporters at a luncheon at the Centre for Strategic and International Studies.
Palestinians insist Israel respect the original timetable under which the pullback should be finished by September.
Ross was expected to meet Arafat on Saturday.
Ashrawi said Ross was urging the Palestinians to accomodate Netanyahu because his fragile governing coalition might shatter if he accepted the original date.
She said that was inappropriate and showed "bias" toward Israel, the Post reported.
"The American role is to make both sides comply with their commitments and honour their agreements and not to apologise for one side or the other," it quoted her as saying.
"I find it objectionable personally that the Americans are trying to justify changes on the basis of domestic political problems for Netanyahu," she continued.

The newspaper quoted State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns as saying Ashrawi's comments were "extraordinarily unwise" and if either side "truly believed that (Ross) was biased, they wouldn't have him at the talks."
